summary: Witness gating is bypass-free and all three review findings are closed: counter tests serialized (0 failures in 600 runs), sentinel corpus guard added, Go identifier in Spanish.
notes: contract-check re-run on the FINAL diff (19 files, +683/-68): ok=true, 0 violations; not_checked: forbid.behaviors (evaluated manually below). All per_class limits respected: canal.rs 173/420, **/tests/** 265/950, Go sentinel 142/260, docs/*.md 10/80, docs/adr/*.md 21/200.
acceptance-coverage status=pass, 0 gaps across AC-1..AC-7. 05-validation.json overall_result=passed; all 7 verify.commands exit 0.

CLOSURE 1 of 3 (blocking defect, VERIFIED BY RE-READ AND RE-RUN): the AC-3 counter race is fixed. crates/hexcell-core/tests/testigo_de_entrante.rs now declares 'static EN_SERIE: Mutex<()>' and both #[test] fns take it poison-tolerantly via unwrap_or_else(|envenenado| envenenado.into_inner()), bound to a named guard (_guardia) so the lock is held for the whole test body rather than dropped at the end of the statement. I rebuilt the test binary and ran it 600 times at --test-threads=4: 0 failures, against the 4 failures in 400 runs at --test-threads=2 I measured before the fix. Scope of the guard is complete: the other hexcell-core integration tests (exhaustividad_resultado_envio.rs, guardian_identidad_conversacion.rs) are separate binaries, hence separate processes with their own copy of the static, so no cross-binary interference exists.

The module doc of testigo_de_entrante.rs was corrected and now states the true premise: asserting deltas protects against ACCUMULATION between tests but not against CONCURRENT increments, with the measured ~1% failure rate cited. That figure matches my own independent measurement, so it is evidence-backed and not a fabricated claim.

CLOSURE 2 of 3 (VERIFIED BY RE-READ AND RE-RUN): the Go sentinel can no longer pass vacuously. detectarLlamadasDeEnvio now returns archivosAnalizados as a second value, incremented only after a successful parser.ParseFile, and TestCentinelaSinRutasDeEnvioFueraDelOutbox t.Fatalfs when it is 0 with a message naming the root path. Ran go test ./internal/outbox/ -run TestCentinela -v: both tests PASS.

CLOSURE 3 of 3 (VERIFIED BY RE-READ): the English identifier 'allowlist' is renamed to 'esRutaDeEnvioVigilada' with a doc comment that now correctly states it recognises the function names whose direct call constitutes a violation, resolving the earlier inverted allowlist/denylist naming. 'interface{}' is also modernised to 'any', and the file-header note lost its parenthetical English term. A grep for 'allowlist' and 'interface{}' in the sentinel returns nothing.

forbid.behaviors manually verified as SATISFIED on every clause: no Cargo/Go dependency added (cargo tree -p hexcell-core still 1 line); variants are struct variants, not tuple variants, with #[non_exhaustive]; the compile_fail doctest is paired with a positive doctest and neither is marked ignore/no_run; no un-witnessed constructor, Default, From<IdConversacion>, rehidratar or para_pruebas escape hatch exists; banco.rs untouched and inyectar_evento not widened; IPC wire untouched; no sidecar send path implemented; the sentinel parses with go/parser + go/ast over a call-name list rather than text-grepping; no existing test deleted, ignored or weakened; D-21 and adr-0021 registered; no Fase B supersession language.

Witness gating verified bypass-free by grepping the whole workspace: TestigoDeEntrante::observar(&EventoEntrante) is the ONLY public witness constructor, the conversacion field is private, and no function anywhere in hexcell-core returns a MensajeSaliente. Every construction site across hexcell, hexcell-storage, hexcell-canal-simulado and hexcell-canal-contrato routes through respuesta_libre/plantilla; the only remaining MensajeSaliente:: mentions outside canal.rs are read-side matches using the mandatory '{ campo, .. }' pattern.

Counter semantics verified: RECHAZOS_DE_CONSTRUCCION.fetch_add sits ONLY on the conversation-mismatch branch of both constructors and never on the Ok path; exposed as pub fn rechazos_de_construccion() -> u64. Note it measures conversation MISMATCH, not 'unwitnessed construction', which is unreachable at runtime by design; the blueprint reframed AC-3 this way and acceptance-coverage accepted it.

Production .expect("la conversacion coincide siempre") at crates/hexcell/src/procesador.rs lines 62 and 107 is provably unreachable: the witness is derived from the same evento whose evento.conversacion is passed as the destination, so the equality always holds. Not a panic risk, and no cfg-less test hook leaked into production code.

Test migrations are honest, not weakened: motor.rs and politica_fuera_de_ventana.rs replace a whole-enum assert_eq! with a let-else destructure plus panic! on the wrong variant plus an assert_eq! on the payload, preserving both the variant and the payload check; persistencia.rs and repositorio_de_sesiones.rs keep their full Vec<EventoDeHistorial> equality assertions.

Go sentinel is non-vacuous in substance, not just by the new guard: the walk root resolves to sidecar/ and visits 10 real non-test .go files, and the sidecar genuinely has zero Send*/Enviar* call sites, confirming AC-6's premise. The synthetic self-test proves the detector still matches a cliente.SendMessage call and that func declarations are not counted.

Docs checked for fabrication: adr-0021, the bitacora D-21 entry and the STATUS line only restate the rustc 1.92.0 mechanics that 07-trace records as empirically verified during the blueprint phase; no unperformed measurement is claimed. docs/adr/README.md gained exactly one row (adr-0021) with no edits to existing rows, and D-21 is correlative after D-20 with a real reopen condition.

RESIDUAL (non-blocking, accepted) - compile_fail hollowness is only partly closed. The negative doctest uses the fully qualified path hexcell_core::canal::MensajeSaliente::RespuestaLibre, but the paired positive doctest never names the RespuestaLibre variant, only the respuesta_libre/plantilla constructors. Renaming the VARIANT would make the compile_fail doctest fail with E0433 instead of E0639 and still report ok, undetected. The contract's literal pairing requirement is met; naming the variant in the positive doctest would close the last gap and is a candidate for A-3 task 12.

RESIDUAL (non-blocking, accepted) - the conversation check binds CONSTRUCTION only, not routing: ChannelAdapter::send takes the conversation separately, so a MensajeSaliente built for conversation A can still be sent to conversation B. This sits outside the spec's stated invariant (no outbound message without an inbound witness), which IS satisfied, but the counter must not be read as a cross-conversation delivery guarantee. Every non-dedicated call site mints its witness from the same conversation it sends to, so the check is a no-op there.

RESIDUAL (non-blocking, accepted) - adr-0021 is thin (20 lines) and its Consecuencias section omits the public API break it introduces: EventoDeHistorial::Saliente changed payload type from MensajeSaliente to SalienteHistorico in hexcell-storage. All in-repo consumers were migrated, so nothing is broken, but a future reader of the ADR will not learn this from it.
Language check: all new Rust and Go identifiers, comments and doc comments are in Spanish and dates are absolute (2026-08-09). No English identifiers remain after closure 3.
